_comment: REQUIRED BY DEFAULT. A registered type binds on EVERY action unless an entry says otherwise, and saying otherwise costs a stated `reason`. The minimal entry {"family": "..."} is the STRICT one -- adding a type is one line and it binds immediately. Inclusion is free; exclusion is the thing that takes effort.
_why: The first draft listed required steps explicitly per action, so adding a checker meant writing it AND remembering to add it to the list. Forget the second half and the checker runs, passes, and counts for nothing -- absence rendering as success, in the very file that defines what complete means. A registry you must remember to extend is a registry that will be incomplete.
_reasonless_narrowing: An `actions` or `when` narrowing with NO `reason` is IGNORED and the type falls back to required-for-all. This is the encoding_whitelist.txt convention, reused deliberately because it is already familiar here: nothing is suppressed until a human has actually looked. A typo in an exemption fails safe.
_unregistered: V8 rejects a record whose step is not listed here, record.py returns None, and the checker exits 2 -- so the pipeline blocks the moment someone wires in an unregistered check, loudly, at the desk of the person who can fix it. That is the pair that closes the hole: you cannot add a check that silently does not count, and you cannot register one that silently is not required.

genesis.reason: the recording floor itself; it is not a gate on any action

build.reason: stub-first commits sorry-stubbed files on purpose, and CI at the PR owns build state; only a release asserts the corpus builds

pdf_coupling.reason: only meaningful when a PDF changed

editorial.reason: prose gate; nothing is published at commit time

adversary.reason: publication gate; nothing is published at commit time

prior_art.reason: publication gate; nothing is published at commit time

rely._why: the /rely round signal. Read by batch.py, ship.py AND guards.py; `rely_cleared.txt` was its only representation, so retiring the signal path without this type deletes the coverage rather than migrating it.

claim_review._why: check_frozen demands it when a BASELINE ENTRY IS REMOVED -- the fail-closed record that an unexamined site had its liability discharged. With no type, deleting a baseline entry becomes free, which is a suppression mechanism losing its price.
claim_review._emitter_contract: MUST be recorded on EVERY run, not only when a baseline entry is removed: PASS when none was, and the discharge record when one was. A key that appears only sometimes is indistinguishable from a key nobody ran -- which is the enumerator-found-nothing defect, and the registry has no way to express 'conditional on an event' (its `when` is a PATH glob).
